claims_about_writeup.quote: the new scientific claim in `contribution.md`, with honest attribution of the steering recipe
claims_about_writeup.why: contribution.md frames the cross-lingual reconstruction as its contribution ("Our contribution is that the direction is a language-invariant processing axis") and explicitly credits Raman et al., 2026 as the source of white-bear steering, matching the claim.
A manual count of contribution.md's prose yields approximately 290 words, matching the stated figure closely enough to be accurate.

differences.what: The message explicitly frames reproducing Raman et al.'s English-only construction as 'out of scope', an explicit novelty/scope justification not stated in the write-up, which only notes the prior construction was English-only without framing reproduction as out of scope.
differences.message_quote: and reproducing it is out of scope
differences.writeup_quote: That direction was constructed only from English benchmark items.

message_source_quote: The reading list's white-bear paper (Raman et al. 2026) showed a large push along the English "think about X while writing" vs "don't think" contrast direction at the concept-formation band L20-24 makes the blocks above write the concept into the read cell — but that construction was only ever done from English benchmark items, and reproducing it is out of scope.
writeup_source_quote: White-bear steering (Raman et al., 2026, reading list) showed that a large push along the mean difference of "think about X while you write" vs "do not think about X while you write" states, injected at L20-24 (the concept-formation band), makes the blocks above write the implied concept into the read cell.
rationale: Both documents name Raman et al., 2026 ("white-bear steering") explicitly and describe the method as building on it by reconstructing its think/don't-think contrast direction in a new language (Spanish, confirmed in French/German), presenting this cross-lingual reconstruction as the novel contribution. The message adds a minor framing not in the write-up—explicitly calling full reproduction of the English-only construction "out of scope"—but otherwise the two documents agree on the source's identity, the overlap (reconstructing the same direction/mechanism), and the claimed novelty (language invariance).
